findings.title: Stream capture has no aggregate retention ceiling
findings.contract: Externally driven capture state must have finite count and combined-byte bounds before copies; this tool captures only one connection through its first request.
findings.cause: streams.setdefault inserts every delivered stream ID, including empty FIN events; only each bytearray has MAX_STREAM_CAPTURE. No entry removal or combined-byte counter exists. Protocol dispatch continues collecting stream events after snapshot_request freezes packet datagrams.
support: run enables optional packet collector only for packet_summary/client_hello output; standalone startup-only CLI leaves packet_capture None.
startup_capture.quic_run always requests client_hello, so its collector has initial packet bounds; this does not cover later events after snapshot_request.finish_datagrams.

Pinned aioquic max_data and stream limits are replenished dynamically (initial max_data1MiB, initial max stream counts128); they are flow-control windows rather than immutable retained-input ceilings.
H3 discards unknown unidirectional stream payloads, while Capture records them before H3.handle_event. Empty FIN produces StreamDataReceived and can create a retained empty dictionary entry.
The thirty-second default timeout and 0.2-second successful grace bound duration, not retained count or total bytes; one active connection reduces exposure but does not establish a hard bound.
findings.remedy: Add concrete retained stream-count and aggregate-byte accounting before inserting/extending. Preserve the existing per-stream ceiling and first-request snapshot contract. Stop further capture mutation after failure and freeze or discard evidence outside the completed boundary without losing still-required startup evidence. Do not infer a cap from aioquic receive-window defaults.
reproduction_plan: Pure event controls: many distinct legal client-initiated stream IDs, each below per-stream ceiling; assert explicit count/aggregate-byte refusal before mutation and a literal small valid positive. Include zero-byte FIN entry growth.

Through CaptureProtocol with real pinned H3 decoder: unknown unidirectional stream types accepted/ignored by H3 must still meet our count/byte boundary; use bounded controlled events or authenticated loopback peer, not invented stream IDs bypassing QUIC legality for an end-to-end claim.

Repeat with packet collector absent, and after first request freezes datagrams; require packet count remains frozen while stream budget refuses extra retention. Preserve existing first-request header/QPACK snapshots byte-for-byte.
findings.evidence_status: supported source finding; no actual memory growth, native leak, benchmark or live-browser reproduction measured
